title: What should you read and listen to for business knowledge before case interviews?
description: Business news, firm insight pages and podcasts that build commercial awareness for case and fit interviews, with a simple daily habit.
hook: Commercial awareness, knowing what is happening in business and why, helps in every part of a case: clarifying questions, hypotheses, brainstorms and fit answers. You do not need hours a day. Fifteen minutes with the right sources is enough.
body:
News

  • Financial Times and The Economist: global business and economics. Many universities provide free access, so check your library.
  • Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg: markets, companies and deals.
  • Your industry's trade press, if you are interviewing for a specialist practice.

The firms' own insights

McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte and others publish free articles and reports on industries and management topics. Reading a few from the firm you are interviewing with also gives you real material for "why this firm".

Podcasts

  • The McKinsey Podcast and HBR IdeaCast: management ideas in short episodes.
  • Acquired: long, detailed histories of companies and how they won.
  • Any business news podcast you enjoy enough to listen to regularly.

A 15-minute daily habit

  1. Read one business story.
  2. Ask: how does this company make money, and what is the "so what"? (The so-what habit.)
  3. Say a 60-second summary out loud, as if to a CEO.
  4. Note one story or example you could use in an interview.
outro: Next in this topic: Where can you find free practice cases from the consulting firms themselves?
